Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, both required skill guides, and the inherited rollout evidence—including both 3D moving-window views—before touching the policy. Then I’ll produce one candidate and update both reasoning files with evidence-backed conclusions.

The workspace confirms this is the common-seed architecture point, so the bookshelf consultation is mandatory. I’ve read both skill contracts; I’m now anchoring the visual review to scores, trajectories, force/flow diagnostics, and inherited optimizer notes before consulting the primitive references.

The evidence now isolates a small but repeatable semantic gain: the parent’s anterior course preview captures at `22.1595T` versus `22.1870T`, with lower mean distance, while keeping the same finite load envelope. The best current sheet has a complete 3D Lambda2 row; the weaker fixed-lead sheet’s oblique row is a render failure, so I’m treating it only as a top-down/numerical control. Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m consulting the mechanism references now; any transfer will remain bounded body-frame state feedback.

The bookshelf supports one compact transfer that matches the evidence: keep the posterior-delayed propulsive carrier intact, but let predicted body-frame route demand recruit a separate bounded anterior redirect. I’ll test that as a new signal-to-actuator allocation—not a gain increase—using the existing proximity and de-yawed line-of-sight observations. First I’m recording the required pre-edit diagnosis and falsification boundaries.

The policy now contains exactly one new mechanism: a proximity-grown, half-cycle preview for the anterior redirect gate; posterior carrier shaping still uses instantaneous geometry, and no authority ceiling or existing gain changed. I’m now folding the completed parent and sibling outcomes into the durable guidance, including the release-only negative result so later workers do not repeat it.

The durable lesson now records the parent’s additive prediction gain and the evaluated release-only regression. I’m invoking the required non-CFD check runner next; if it finds any provenance, schema, finite-output, equivariance, or boundary issue, I’ll repair and rerun it.

The configured check runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. The invocation requirement is satisfied; I’m running the TOML’s exact non-CFD checks directly and will treat any failure the same way.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` lists the same guidance example twice as the copied parent, so provenance is ambiguous. I’m removing the duplicate line (matching the inherited parent log’s intended repair) and rerunning the guidance check.

All three prescribed checks now pass: guidance provenance/materiality, finite two-joint policy output, and solver-boundary integrity. I’m doing one final static/schema and symmetry audit—still no CFD—to ensure the new parameter is owned and the body-frame feedback remains reflection-equivariant.

Final verification is clean: one candidate file exists, every `params.FIELD` reference is owned, finite output and reflection equivariance pass, guidance materiality passes, and the solver boundary passes. No CFD was run, as required.

Completed exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:23) adds a bounded, proximity-gated half-cycle preview exclusively to anterior-redirect recruitment.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:5) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:259) adds the reusable predictive-allocation lesson and release-only negative result.
- Removed the duplicate parent marker in [README.md](README.md:123).

Guidance materiality, parameter schema, finite output, reflection equivariance, and boundary checks pass. The configured checker model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
